sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage establishes that God, having spoken through the prophets in many fragments and modes, has now spoken his final and unified word through the Son in these last days.

The neutral reading identifies seven characterizations of the Son -- heir, creator, radiance, exact impress, sustainer, purifier of sins, enthroned king -- as establishing the Son's comprehensive identity and cosmic role.
The neutral reading identifies this verse as the thesis statement: the Son has become superior to the angels and has inherited a more excellent name than they.
The neutral reading shows this section pairs Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14 to demonstrate that the title 'Son' -- a messianic, Davidic designation -- was never given to any angel.
The neutral reading finds this citation from Deuteronomy 32:43 or Psalm 97:7 establishes that God commands the angels to worship the Son, placing the Son in the position of the one worshiped.

sections.section_title: What Angels Are and What the Son Is
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the contrast between angels as changeable created servants (Psalm 104:4) and the Son who is addressed as God with an eternal throne and anointed above his companions (Psalm 45:6-7).

sections.section_title: The Son as Creator, Creation as Perishable
sections.summary: The neutral reading shows the author applies Psalm 102:25-27 -- a text originally addressed to YHWH as unchanging creator -- to the Son, establishing his permanence in contrast to the perishability of creation.

The neutral reading finds this section completes the Son-angel hierarchy by citing Psalm 110:1 (the Son sits at God's right hand) while identifying angels as ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.
